is one which has been formed from two or more atomic propositions using logical connectives.
The truth value of a compound proposition depends upon the truth values of its component atomic propositions.
All non-atomic propositions are compound propositions.

For example: ‘I am a student at university, and I am studying for a maths degree’ is a compound proposition. It is constructed from two atomic propositions: ‘I am a student at university’ and ‘I am studying for a maths degree’.

children.value: We say that if a proposition is true then its negation is false, and if the proposition is false then its negation is true.
For example, let p represent the proposition “There is a bug in the program”. Then,

children.html: p̸\not pp

children.value: stands for the proposition “It is not the case that there is a bug in the program”, or “There is not a bug in the program”.

This plus some other better examples
Find the negation of the proposition “Michael’s PC runs Linux” and express this in simple English.
Solution: The negation is “It is not the case that Michael’s PC runs Linux.”
This negation can be more simply expressed as “Michael’s PC does not run Linux.”
